minutes.headline: Board reviewed a proposed storm water utility fee bylaw headed to spring Town Meeting, split public reaction
minutes.summary: The Select Board ratified two new police sergeants, approved a pavilion dedication and a teen center fundraiser, and heard a lengthy joint presentation with the Planning Board and Storm Water Task Force on a proposed storm water utility bylaw and fee for spring Town Meeting. The Town Manager reported on FY27 budget preparation, building consolidation plans, and staffing, and the Board discussed warrant articles including possibly dropping the mosquito control program and legislative earmark requests; recurring public comment came from a resident opposing the storm water utility and from a family alleging town retaliation over an HOA-payment records request.

attendees.role: director of planning and economic development

public_comment.topic: Opposes a separate storm water utility/fee; wants the federal mandate funded within the regular budget.
Alleges town persecution of his family tied to a public records request about a town payment to the Village at Flat Hill HOA.

public_comment.stated_role: resident, 105 Chestnut Street, civil engineer and commercial property owner
public_comment.topic: Supports a storm water utility in principle but raises cost and timing concerns for businesses and asks how future rate increases would be set.
Says the utility creates unnecessary bureaucracy and prefers funding storm water through the regular budget.
Asks how the storm water utility would apply to a homeowners association's privately maintained roads.
Final comment that she still does not see the benefits ("pros") of the storm water utility.
Thanks the presenters and offers to discuss his HOA's storm water/wastewater situation with them.

public_comment.stated_role: resident, 39 Courtland Circle, representing his family
public_comment.topic: Continues allegations about the HOA payment records, complains about a promoted officer's past conduct, and asks about a lawsuit involving water contamination; says he will continue at the next meeting.

votes.motion: Ratify the appointments of Christopher Berseron and Anthony Kapuchi to sergeant, Lunenburg Police Department, effective February 10, 2026.
Approve the boot drive application for the Club Lunenburg Teen Center, Saturday May 30, 2026, 10am-2pm.
Approve the request to dedicate the Adult Activity Center pavilion in honor of Peter and Deborah Lincoln.
Authorize the chair/town manager to sign the DLTA grant application letter to the regional planning commission.
Create a cable advisory committee (two PAC members, one select board member, two at-large members) to initiate the cable ascertainment process for the Comcast contract renewal.
Designate Amanda Moore as the select board's representative to the cable advisory committee.
Ratify the town manager's appointment of Mark Richardy to Council on Aging van driver.

budget_items.topic: Club Lunenburg Teen Center boot drive scholarships
budget_items.what_was_said: A staff member said the summer program awarded scholarships to disadvantaged kids, funded entirely by the voluntary road toll and other events.
The planning director said the town's in-kind match for the mapping and housing production plan projects is his staff time, and estimated the value of the grant-funded work to the town.

budget_items.topic: Storm water utility budget / MS4 compliance cost
budget_items.what_was_said: The DPW director estimated the additional annual cost to get into MS4 permit compliance, on top of what is already budgeted.
figures_as_heard: the 110,000 that's currently in the budget

budget_items.topic: Storm water utility fee vs. override
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member said adding the compliance cost to the operating budget would force an override, comparing the estimated fee and override impact per household.
The town manager said the underused ClearGov budgeting software subscription was cancelled due to budget and staffing constraints.

budget_items.topic: Adult Activity Center IT/network capital item and grant
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager said a capital request for network upgrades at the AAC was unlikely to be funded in the capital plan, so she applied for a Community Compact IT grant instead.

budget_items.topic: Legislative earmark requests for FY27 state budget
budget_items.what_was_said: Board members proposed earmark requests for fire department equipment, an accessibility ramp/telehealth space at the Adult Activity Center, and design work for a playground at the primary school.

budget_items.topic: Central Mass Mosquito Control Program assessment
budget_items.what_was_said: A member raised the town's mosquito control assessment for possible warrant article consideration, comparing it to other communities' costs.
The board of assessors report said the board signed the FY26 motor vehicle excise commitment.
A member relayed the school committee's FY27 level-service and restoration budget figures and health insurance cost increase, plus the FY26 comparison.
The school committee report noted concerns about special education capacity after prior budget cuts, with a number of students currently placed out of district.

budget_items.topic: Repurposed van earmark for Turkey Hill ADA bathrooms
budget_items.what_was_said: The school committee authorized the superintendent to explore repurposing a prior earmark meant for vans toward ADA bathroom upgrades at Turkey Hill.
The finance committee report said Monty Tech presented a preliminary FY27 assessment showing a large percentage increase, consistent with the town's own estimate.

decisions.decision: Town manager will meet with Mr. Franco Friday to work through senior tax relief warrant article concerns and bring something back to the board.
Warrant article submission deadline for other boards/committees confirmed as March 16.
Board agreed to remove the sentence requiring a written statement of reasons for requesting interviews from the appointment policy draft.
Board agreed to fix wording in the reappointment policy so the town manager's office forwards the 'completed' reappoint application.
Board agreed the town manager can engage the Board of Health on the mosquito control question and seek a presentation from the mosquito control program (and possibly an opposing viewpoint).
Next storm water public information session confirmed for March 5 at the library, 6:30-8:00 p.m.
No select board meeting scheduled the week of February 17 due to school vacation.

what_happened.line: Board and Planning Board heard a joint presentation on a proposed storm water utility bylaw and fee for spring Town Meeting, with mixed public reaction on cost and HOA road applicability.
Board ratified two new police sergeants and formed a cable advisory committee to begin Comcast contract renewal talks.
Town manager reported on FY27 budget preparation and said the town cancelled its ClearGov budgeting software subscription over cost and staffing constraints.
Board asked the town manager to bring the Board of Health and a mosquito-control program presentation back before deciding whether to drop that assessment from a warrant article.
A family repeated allegations of town retaliation tied to a records request about a payment to a homeowners association, unresolved for a second time this meeting.

why_it_matters: The storm water utility, if adopted at spring Town Meeting, would likely appear as a separate fee rather than folded into the tax-funded operating budget, and a board member compared that fee against what an override for the same cost would mean per household.
Cutting the Central Mass Mosquito Control assessment from the FY27 warrant is now an open question the town manager will bring back with input from the Board of Health.
The cancelled ClearGov subscription and the FY27 budget prep discussion touch how the town builds and explains next year's budget to residents.
watch_next: Storm water utility public information session, March 5, library, 6:30-8:00 p.m.
Warrant article submission deadline for other boards/committees, March 16

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on outcomes: every vote total, dollar figure, and procedural decision we captured matches the official minutes once caption-garbled names and digits are resolved. The one thing a reader should check first is that Member Glenn McLeod — a voting board member who cast the abstentions and gave the Planning Board report — is entirely absent from our attendee list, and that the official minutes reference a "February 17 meeting" Lehtinen would miss, which contradicts our note that no meeting was scheduled that week.
